reviewer: Codex, a separate model review from DeepSeek proof generation; same operator assistant that prepared the harness, not a blinded human reviewer
scope: All 11 assigned PDF pages visually inspected and independently text-extracted; source definitions, numbered results/exercises, operative body claims and Notes compared with final Lean declaration statements and relevant definitions.
prior_kernel_evidence: Release build and 150-declaration axiom check previously passed; no unchanged full build rerun solely for this audit.
new_kernel_evidence: Elaborated chapter signatures read and six independent domain/convention-check lemmas compiled, with standard axioms only.
verdict: Core main theorem statements broadly correspond under documented finite-domain/nondegeneracy conventions. Literal full-source correspondence is not certified: one mathematical Notes claim is omitted and domain/scope/bridge findings remain.
not_found: No incorrect main numbered theorem statement, custom theorem axiom or convergence-valued circular assumption identified in the reviewed final targets. This is not a proof of absence of every possible specification defect.
limitations: Not blinded: reviewer had earlier experiment context.
No line-by-line mathematical reproof of every helper; kernel evidence is used for proof validity.
No new lower-bound theorem or corrected experimental proof was supplied.
Finite-domain scope choices are distinguished from false statements; source-silent assumptions require an explicit acceptance policy.

findings.impact: Material to an unrestricted source-completeness claim; not a falsified finite-domain theorem
findings.source: Book p.5: expectation, variance, moments and MGF; p.7 explicitly allows infinite nonnegative expectations.
findings.finding: The exported expectation/moment/MGF wrappers return real Bochner integrals. Outside Integrable, the integral returns 0. The imported real variance similarly returns 0 outside MemLp 2 rather than representing infinite variance. No domain predicate or extended-valued MGF wrapper accompanies the exported MGF definition.
findings.evidence: Six separate audit lemmas compile against the release: nonintegrable expectation and exponential expectation equal 0; measurable non-L2 real variance equals 0 while extended variance is infinity; Real.rpow (-1) (1/3) equals 1/2 and the constant-variable HDP.moment equals 1/2. The last example illustrates a convention issue, not a failure of integer or absolute moments. See evidence/Chapter01DomainChecks.lean and its compiler output.
findings.qualification: Standard totalization used by Mathlib is legitimate inside the proper domain. The main limit theorems have integrability/MemLp hypotheses protecting them. The nonnegative layer-cake and Markov statements also have extended-valued versions. This is a representation/domain finding, not proof unsoundness.
findings.closure: State and justify a finite-domain convention, document the MGF integrability domain, or add an extended-valued representation and a correspondence theorem. Do not count an unrestricted real wrapper as a literal representation at divergent inputs. For ordinary moments, restrict the exponent/domain or explicitly justify the negative-base real-power convention.

findings.impact: Requires an explicit source interpretation or an extended-value completion
findings.source: Book p.7, Exercise 1.2.2: signed tail identity for any random variable.
findings.finding: integral_eq_tail_sub_lower requires Integrable X. It proves the finite signed expectation identity, not the one-sided infinite cases that a literal extended-expectation reading can include.
findings.qualification: For absolutely integrable variables, this statement matches; the change from Iio 0 to Iic 0 affects only a Lebesgue-null endpoint. The source does not define infinity-minus-infinity, so not every measurable variable has a meaningful signed identity. The extra integrability hypothesis is reasonable under a finite-quantity convention but must be disclosed.
findings.closure: Explicitly adopt the integrable reading or handle the extended cases where at least one signed part has finite integral.

findings.impact: Finite-second-moment exercise versions; not the broadest meaningful extended reading
findings.finding: Both variance identities require MemLp 2. The book does not explicitly impose finite second moments; for integrable vectors with infinite second moment, the corresponding nonnegative expectations can have a meaningful extended-value identity.
findings.qualification: The finite-second-moment statements are correct, and the empirical-method application uses a finite bounded sampling distribution, so this restriction does not undermine approximate Caratheodory or the covering bounds. The book itself needs an existence convention for E Z.
findings.closure: Report these exercises as finite-second-moment versions, or supply appropriately stated extended identities. Do not treat source-silent moment assumptions as an exact unqualified transcription.

findings.impact: Definite omission under the experiment protocol including mathematical claims in Notes
findings.source: Book p.4, Notes 0.0.1, final sentence: the Exercise 0.0.6 bound is asserted sharp.
findings.finding: improved_covering supplies an upper covering bound with constant 4. The only sharpness theorem in the final Appetizer source concerns the n+1 Caratheodory bound. No lower-bound/optimality statement for Exercise 0.0.6 is formalized. The model inventory incorrectly treats the Notes as having no mathematical assertion.
findings.qualification: The source gives a citation and no precise lower-bound quantifiers or parameter regime. A faithful new target requires specifying what sharp means in that cited assertion. Omitting historical bibliography is reasonable; omitting this mathematical assertion needs a separate explicit scope exclusion.
findings.closure: Either restrict the completion claim to the specified numbered results and finite-domain exercises, excluding cited optimality, or specify and formalize the sharpness assertion with appropriate source evidence.

findings.impact: Canonical definition is valid; generic source-family identification is not established locally
findings.source: Book p.10: the sum S_N of the independent Bernoulli family has Binom(N,p) distribution.
findings.finding: binomialMeasure is defined as the law of the coordinate sum under a canonical product of Bernoulli measures. No theorem identifies the sum of an arbitrary independent Bernoulli family with this measure. The separately retained binomialPMFMeasure is not linked to it either.
findings.qualification: The canonical product-law definition is mathematically sound and can be accepted as a definition of the distribution. The source does not state the binomial PMF, so equivalence to that PMF is not by itself a missing book theorem. The bridge for an arbitrary source family is the relevant correspondence issue. De Moivre-Laplace is proved directly for arbitrary independent Bernoulli variables and is not invalidated.
findings.closure: Add the generic map-of-sum equality, or explicitly classify this row as a canonical distribution definition rather than a proved law-identification theorem.

findings.impact: Misleading exported draft names; no defect found in the proved limit theorems
findings.source: Book pp.9-10: independent identically distributed sequences and independent Bernoulli rows.
findings.finding: The historical IsIID definition uses pairwise independence. The retained draft CLT/de Moivre/Poisson targets therefore do not encode the intended full joint-independence specification. They are still imported/exported by HDP.lean.
findings.qualification: These are Prop definitions, not proofs; the file header and release README label them historical. The actual central_limit_theorem and de_moivre_laplace use iIndepFun; poisson_limit_theorem uses iIndepFun within each finite row. Those proved statements do not inherit the draft error.
findings.closure: Move the drafts outside the public final library or rename them clearly as historical specifications. Keep their existence separate from completion/axiom claims.

chapter01_comparison.source_item: pp.5-6 Lp norm and Lp membership
chapter01_comparison.assessment: eLpNorm has the intended positive finite exponent/infinity meaning; MemLp adds measurability as random-variable structure. Raw functions are identified a.e. in the Banach-space interpretation.
CompleteSpace and InnerProductSpace of Mathlib Lp are the appropriate quotient-space structures; not new independent analytic proofs.
Integral of XY, centered covariance and the sqrt-variance/norm identity. L2 hypotheses prevent default-value problems.
A two-point probability-space counterexample for every real exponent in (0,1), not merely p=1/2.
Global convexity and integrability of X and phi(X). Infinite RHS version not separately stated; disclose finite-domain convention.
Probability measure and measurable X; eLpNorm order. The source defines Lp only for p>0, so p=0 is a totalization convention, not a substantive target.
p>=1, X,Y in MemLp, including p=infinity.
Absolute expected product; finite conjugates and the 1/infinity endpoint covered.
<= for CDF and strict > for upper tail, with the correct complement probability.
Real integrable and ENNReal versions together cover simultaneous finiteness/infinity.
Matches the absolutely integrable case; one-sided infinite cases need scope treatment.
All p>0; real equality under finiteness of extended RHS, plus the extended identity. On a probability space this matches the source finiteness condition.
Finite real and extended-value threshold inequalities, positive t, nonnegative random variable.
Correct centered absolute tail, t^2 denominator and proof via Markov on the square.
Pairwise independence suffices; MemLp 2, identical distributions and positive N give the correct sample-mean variance.
Integrable common law, a.e. sample-mean convergence, pairwise independence is a valid weakening here. Zero-based indices have no mathematical effect.
Correct standard normal PDF formula; the measure/density interpretation relies on the imported Gaussian library.
Mutual iIndepFun, common distribution, finite second moments, actual mean and variance. sigma>0 is needed for the source normalization. No desired-convergence hypothesis is assumed.

chapter01_comparison.source_item: p.9 CLT CDF and tail restatement
chapter01_comparison.assessment: All real thresholds; correct Iic/Ici events. Limit is Gaussian half-line measure. The final explicit density-integral display is not restated in one local theorem but follows from the library density representation.
Expected absolute deviation is O(1/sqrt(N)); finite variance, a weaker pairwise-independence hypothesis is sufficient.

chapter01_comparison.source_item: p.10 Bernoulli law, mean and variance
chapter01_comparison.assessment: Correct masses at 0/1 and p(1-p), with p in [0,1].
Canonical product-law definition is valid; arbitrary independent-family bridge is absent.
p in (0,1), arbitrary jointly independent Bernoulli sequence, centered normalized law converges to N(0,1). Algebraically equivalent source normalization.
Correct Poisson PMF on naturals; pushforward to real line used for weak convergence, including lambda=0.
Joint independence within each finite row, uniform maximum tending to 0, sum of p tending to finite lambda>=0; convergence of actual sum laws. No conclusion-valued assumption.
Not proved theorems, not accepted target evidence; actual final CLT and Poisson statements use correct independence.
Bibliography and attribution are narrative. Geometric covariance interpretation is explained by the checked inner-product identity; the later-chapter forward reference is outside scope.
